newsDocuments.headline: Iran says five tankers and tugboat caught fire in Hormuz

segments.text: TEHRAN: Five oil tankers and a tugboat caught fire in the Strait of Hormuz, Iran’s Revolutionary Guards and army said in separate statements, according to local media on Thursday.
Since the outbreak of the Iran war in late February, Tehran has severely restricted traffic through the strategic waterway, which normally carries about one-fifth of global oil consumption.

“Last night… a large oil tanker attempting to pass through the illegal passageway south of the Strait of Hormuz suffered a fire after striking a mine and was brought to a halt,” the Guards told Fars news agency.

newsDocuments.headline: Soybeans and corn firm on higher oil prices, but set for weekly losses

segments.text: SINGAPORE: Soybeans and corn rose on Friday as gains in oil prices supported agricultural goods, although expectations of ample global supplies limited the upside and left both markets on track for weekly losses.
“Oil is bit supportive but we don’t expect a big move before next week’s US report.”
On Friday, grains and oilseeds were underpinned by a rally in crude oil futures, which often provide direction to farm goods for their growing use in making biofuels.

newsDocuments.headline: Oil set for sharp weekly drop but Middle East supply concerns provide floor

segments.text: BEIJING/PERTH: Oil prices are set for a sharp weekly drop on expectations of a de-escalation of the Iran war after US President Donald Trump’s party suffered election losses, but Middle East supply concerns from the conflict continue to pro
Brent crude futures for January rose on Friday by $1.29, or 1.31%, to $99.58 a barrel as of 0504 GMT.
US West Texas Intermediate futures climbed 86 cents, or 0.95%, to $91.38 a barrel.

newsDocuments.headline: Japan rubber future rise as tight supply trumps oil slide

segments.text: TOKYO: Japanese rubber futures edged higher on Thursday, as tight supply outweighed the impact of a steep slide in oil prices.

Oil prices fell for a fourth day on Thursday on expectations the losses US President Donald Trump’s Republican Party suffered in Congressional elections this week may reduce the risk of further escalation of the US-Israeli war on Iran.
Natural rubber often takes direction from oil prices as it competes for market share with synthetic rubber, which is made from crude oil.
